title: A scheme over a field covered by finitely many finite open pieces is finite, of degree at most the sum
statement: Let $k$ be a field, let $T$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] with a morphism $t:T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and let $T=W_1\cup\dots\cup W_m$ ($m\ge0$) be a covering of $T$ by finitely many open subschemes. Suppose that for each $i$ the scheme $W_i$, over $k$ through $t|_{W_i}$, is finite over $k$ [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] (so $W_i$ is affine and $\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O_{W_i})$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-algebra) with $\dim_k\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O_{W_i})\le n_i$ for an integer $n_i\ge0$. Then $T$ is finite over $k$ and $\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)\le n_1+\dots+n_m$. (The step 'if $n_i$ works for $f|_{U_i}:U_i\to V_i$, then $\sum n_i$ works for $f$' of the proof of Stacks Project, Morphisms, Lemma Tag 03JA, applied to the fibre $T=X_y$ and its open covering by the fibres $(U_i)_y$.)

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded), first paragraph, lines 15505-15518 (stated without proof there; compare the proofs of Lemma Tag 03J5, line 15322, and Tag 03J6, line 15371: a scheme over a field with finite discrete underlying space is affine and its ring is the product of its local rings)

proof.text: *The pieces.* Fix $i$ and put $B_i=\Gamma(W_i,\mathcal O_{W_i})$, a $k$-algebra through the ring map $k=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathcal O)\to B_i$ induced by the structure morphism $t_i=t\circ\iota_i$ of $W_i$ ($\iota_i:W_i\to T$ the inclusion of the open subscheme). Since $t_i$ is finite, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-field-affine-finite-dim] shows that $W_i$ is affine, the canonical morphism $W_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is an isomorphism (in particular a homeomorphism of underlying spaces), and $B_i$ is finite-dimensional over $k$, with $\dim_kB_i\le n_i$ by hypothesis. The field $k$ is a local ring whose only prime ideal is $(0)$, and $B_i$ is a finite $k$-algebra, so by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-over-zero-dim-local-discrete-spectrum] $\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ is a finite discrete space. Hence the underlying space of $W_i$ is finite and discrete: it has finitely many points and every point $w\in W_i$ has $\{w\}$ open in $W_i$.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371 ff.: 'the underlying topological space of $Y_z$ is a finite discrete set' and 'Thus $X_z$ is an affine scheme' (the same argument, used here for $T$)

proof.text: *$T$ is finite and discrete.* As a set $T=W_1\cup\dots\cup W_m$ is a finite union of finite sets (step 1), hence finite (empty when $m=0$). Let $x\in T$; choose $i$ with $x\in W_i$. By step 1, $\{x\}$ is open in the subspace $W_i$, and $W_i$ is open in $T$ (an open subscheme [def-pc-scheme] has an open underlying set carrying the subspace topology), so $\{x\}$ is open in $T$. Every subset of $T$ is the union of its points, hence open: $T$ is discrete.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371 ff.: 'the underlying topological space of $Y_z$ is a finite discrete set' and 'Thus $X_z$ is an affine scheme' (the same argument, used here for $T$)

proof.text: *$T$ is affine.* By step 2 and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-discrete-scheme-affine], $T$ is affine: with $A=\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$ the canonical morphism $T\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is an isomorphism. Make $A$ a $k$-algebra through the ring map $t^\sharp:k=\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathcal O)\to A$ induced by $t$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03J6 (lemma-composition-universally-bounded), line 15371 ff.: 'the underlying topological space of $Y_z$ is a finite discrete set' and 'Thus $X_z$ is an affine scheme' (the same argument, used here for $T$)

proof.text: *Injection into the product of the pieces.* Let $\rho_i:A=\mathcal O_T(T)\to\mathcal O_T(W_i)=B_i$ be the restriction map; it is the map induced on global sections by the open immersion $\iota_i$. Since global sections are functorial, the ring map $k\to B_i$ induced by $t_i=t\circ\iota_i$ is $\rho_i\circ t^\sharp$, so $\rho_i$ is a homomorphism of $k$-algebras, and $\rho=(\rho_1,\dots,\rho_m):A\to\prod_{i=1}^mB_i$ is $k$-linear. It is injective: if $\rho(s)=0$, then the section $s$ of the sheaf $\mathcal O_T$ [def-pc-scheme] restricts to $0$ on every member of the open covering $T=\bigcup_iW_i$, so $s=0$ by the identity (locality) axiom of a sheaf. (For $m=0$, $T=\emptyset$ and $A=\mathcal O_T(\emptyset)=0$, the empty product.) Hence $\dim_kA\le\dim_k\prod_iB_i=\sum_i\dim_kB_i\le n_1+\dots+n_m$; in particular $A$ is a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space, i.e. a finitely generated $k$-module.

source.place: Morphisms, proof of Lemma Tag 03JA (lemma-locally-quasi-finite-qc-source-universally-bounded), lines 15507-15518: 'if $n_i$ works for the morphism $f|_{U_i}$, then $\sum n_i$ works for $f$' (stated without proof)

proof.text: *$T$ is finite over $k$.* Cover $\operatorname{Spec}k$ by the single affine open $\operatorname{Spec}k$ itself [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Its preimage $t^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}k)=T$ is affine (step 3), and the ring map $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k,\mathcal O)=k\to\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=A$ induced by $t$ makes $A$ a finitely generated $k$-module (step 4). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-local-on-target] ((2)$\Rightarrow$(1)), $t$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], i.e. $T$ is finite over $k$, and by step 4 its degree is $\dim_k\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)=\dim_kA\le n_1+\dots+n_m$.
